Locate points or addresses

Source: R/locate.R
gcd_locate.Rd

The county, 2020 Census tract and block group, school district and zoned schools that points or street addresses fall in.

Points are sent to the API's POST /locate route in batches of up to 1,000, so coordinates never appear in URLs and nothing is cached. Addresses never reach the Georgia Civic Data API: the package geocodes them on your computer with the U.S. Census batch geocoder (https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/, benchmark Public_AR_Current, the address data the API's own search uses; up to 10,000 addresses per upload), then sends the coordinates as points. An address the Census can't match is never sent. To geocode with another service, geocode first (for example with the 'tidygeocoder' package) and pass lat and lon.

A zone is the default assignment, not the only option: a student may attend another public school by transfer, or a charter, magnet or other choice school. This is not an official enrollment determination; confirm with the school district.

Usage

gcd_locate(
  lat = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  address = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  grade = NULL,
  year = NULL
)

Arguments

lat, lon

Numeric vectors of equal length: latitude and longitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). Default NULL.

address

Street addresses: a character vector of one-line addresses ("206 Washington St SW, Atlanta, GA 30334"), or a data frame with columns street, city, state and zip. Give either lat and lon or address, not both. Default NULL.

id

Identifiers for the inputs, the same length, carried into the output so results join back to your data. Default seq_along() of the input.

grade

Keep only school zones serving this grade ("pk", "k", "01" to "12"; "5" and "K" are accepted). Default NULL: every grade.

year

The zones' school year as its ending year (2027 is 2026-27). Default NULL: the current zones.

Value

A tibble with columns, in order:

  1. id.

  2. The input: lat, lon for points; for addresses address, the geocoder's match_status ("match", "no_match", "tie"), match_type ("exact", "non_exact"), matched_address, and the geocoded lat and lon.

  3. geographic_type: "county", "tract", "block_group", "school_district", "elementary_school", "middle_school" or "high_school".

  4. geographic_id: county FIPS ("13121"), tract GEOID ("13121003500"), block group GEOID ("131210035001"), district code ("761"), or for a school "DISTRICT-SCHOOL" ("761-4560"), the form gcd_rows() takes as school_id.

  5. geographic_name: the place's name.

  6. grades: a school row's grade range ("K-5", "6-8", "9-12"); NA on other rows.

  7. note: NA, or why a row is missing or needs care.

Attributes assignment_note and note carry the API's notes on reading the zones.

Output

A long tibble: for each input, one row per place it falls in. A typical location gives seven rows: its county, tract, block group and school district, then one row per zoned school. Rows for each input come in a fixed order: county, tract, block group, district, then elementary, middle and high schools by grade.

A level can have more than one school row: some homes are zoned to one elementary school for kindergarten to grade 2 and another for grades 3-5. The grades column tells them apart; pass grade to keep only the school for one grade.

The note column is NA normally, and one plain sentence otherwise, so a missing row is never silent:

  • a level with no zone collected yet, a gap between zones, or a level served by another district gets a row with NA id, name and grades, and a note saying why;

  • an input outside Georgia, a point the API rejects, or an address the Census can't match gets one row with NA geographic columns and the reason; one bad input never stops the batch;

  • in a Department of Defense district the district row has an NA id and a note;

  • school rows whose zone has a known pending change, or which overlap another school's zone, say so.

See also

gcd_school_zones() for the zones' shapes and precision (method, accuracy_class); gcd_rows() with school_id for data on a located school.

Other geography: gcd_district_boundaries(), gcd_school_zone_coverage(), gcd_school_zone_status(), gcd_school_zones()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# The Georgia State Capitol, by coordinates and by address
gcd_locate(lat = 33.7490, lon = -84.3880)
gcd_locate(address = "206 Washington St SW, Atlanta, GA 30334")

# Only the school for one grade
gcd_locate(lat = 33.7490, lon = -84.3880, grade = "9")
}
